newsitem.title: CHINA: China underwear firm's logo up in smoke.
newsitem.headline: China underwear firm's logo up in smoke.

text.p: A major Chinese underwear producer has responded to a nationwide anti-smoking campaign by removing the pipe from the lips of its old man logo.

Underwear producer Milaoda Group Co splashed out 250,000 yuan ($30,120) on a full-page advertisment in Wednesday's edition of the Communist Party mouthpiece People's Daily to announce the logo change.
The company's symbol, published in the newspaper, remains the head of an old man -- but the pipe that used to protrude from his mouth is gone.

"The change is a response to the nationwide anti-smoking campaign," a Milaoda official told Reuters. "We produce cotton and woollen products and it is not so good for such products to be associated with smoke and fire," she said.
The company also wanted to make their logo more distinct from those of other firms that used similar images of old men with pipes, she said.

"Our company has recently been promoted to a national group company from a city company, so we changed the symbol at this time," she added. "We don't think it will have a negative influence on our sales because it is just a small change."
